sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain by Leo Moll. “Spiel’ mir auf der Balalaika einen russischen Tango.” Tango; label credits Dr. B. Kaper and Fritz Rotter. Electrola E.G. 2392, label number 60-1717; issued October 1931. Disc label shown in the YouTube transfer published by Grammophonics – 78Upm.
sources.title: Spiel’ mir auf der Balalaika einen russischen Tango — Electrola E.G. 2392
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Leo Moll, vocal refrain
sources.researchNote: The displayed label identifies Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain singer Leo Moll, Electrola E.G. 2392 and number 60-1717. Henry König’s Electrola label list supplies matrix “00499-1”, a Berlin session on 18 August 1931 and release in October 1931, citing Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, vol. 2; it also lists HMV AM 3741. The structured date describes the catalogue issue, not the session or manufacture of this copy. The earlier archive caption’s 1932 was incorrect. No Wiener Boheme-Verlag publisher credit appears on the displayed label.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Austin Egen. “Tränen weint jede Frau so gern.” Tango. Digital transfer on YouTube; the upload identifies His Master’s Voice / Electrola and gives the year as 1929.
sources.title: Tränen weint jede Frau so gern — Marek Weber, YouTube
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refraingesang: Austin Egen
sources.researchNote: The upload identifies Marek Weber und sein Orchester with Austin Egen, a His Master’s Voice / Electrola issue and the year 1929, but supplies no catalogue or matrix number and does not show the disc label. It does not distinguish recording from issue year. Nico Dostal’s arrangement credit, Kaper’s music credit and Fritz Rotter’s words credit are uploader-supplied, not label transcriptions. The separate Tauber session documented for the same song does not identify this Weber transfer.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola E.G. 2271, “Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich”
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester. “Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich.” Tango; label credits Dr. Kaper and German, with words by Fritz Rotter. Electrola E.G. 2271, label number 60-1520; issued June 1931. Disc label shown in the YouTube transfer published by 78rpm Musik.
sources.title: Du lieber Geiger, spiel’ einen Tango für mich — Electrola E.G. 2271
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester
sources.researchNote: The displayed label reads “Tanz-Orchester mit Refraingesang”, identifies Marek Weber und sein Orchester and gives E.G. 2271 and 60-1520. The earlier statement that no label was shown was incorrect. Henry König’s Electrola label list supplies matrix OD267-1, a session at the Berlin Electrola studio on 24 March 1931 and release in June 1931, citing Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, p. 2526. The list describes the side as “Instr.”, in conflict with the wording on the label itself, not merely with the uploader’s description. The discrepancy remains unresolved; no refrain singer is identified here. The structured date describes the catalogue issue, not a session or the manufacture of the photographed copy; the catalogued take is not confirmed from the visible runout.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain credited as Leo Moll. “Signorina aus Brioni.” Tango; label credits Fritz Rotter and Dr. Kaper for music and text. Electrola E.G. 2400, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Signorina aus Brioni — Electrola E.G. 2400
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Refrain: Leo Moll
sources.researchNote: The uploader identifies the singer credited as Leo Moll as Leo Monosson and reports 1931 as the Electrola issue year. Neither that identification nor the issue year is printed on the filmed label; the year remains reported, without a newly established session date. The accompanying 1930 photograph depicts Brioni and does not date the disc. Discographic entries for other performers’ recordings of this song are not used to date Electrola E.G. 2400. The examined label names no sheet-music publisher; Edition Karl Brüll is documented by a separate printed source.

sources.shortCitation: YouTube, “Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation” — uploader-identified recording
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, vocal by John Hendrik. “Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation.” Tango. Digital transfer on YouTube; the uploader identifies Electrola E.G. 2508 and gives the year as 1932.
sources.title: Du bist in meinem Leben die erste Sensation — external listening reference
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Gesang: John Hendrik
sources.researchNote: An uploader-created opening card gives Electrola E.G. 2508, matrix E-OD 795 / I and a recording date of 17 February 1932. The disc label is not shown and the card contains no authorship credits. The Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de instead lists E.G. 2508 against “Spanischer Zigeunertanz” (OD 773-1) and “Die alte Spieluhr” (OD770-1), not this title. These descriptions conflict; the upload has not been identified with a verified historical pressing. Its year and performer details remain uploader-supplied, and it is retained as a listening reference rather than a verified description of E.G. 2508.

additionalLinks.label: Electrola label list — conflicting catalogue-number evidence

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, dance orchestra with refrain vocal. “Margarete, wander mit mir ….” Fox-trot; label credits music and text to Fritz Rotter and Dr. B. Kaper. Electrola E.G. 2406, label number 60-1740, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Margarete, wander mit mir … — Electrola E.G. 2406
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Tanz-Orchester mit Refraingesang
sources.researchNote: The filmed label identifies Marek Weber und sein Orchester, Electrola E.G. 2406 and the printed number 60-1740. That number is transcribed as a label number, not an independently verified matrix or take. R. Pfau’s Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 6, printed p. 736, independently lists “EG 2406 Marek Weber” under “Margarethe wander mit mir”. Its general year 1931 is not a separately documented session or issue date. The source retains 1931 as the uploader-reported recording year. The uploader’s link to an Italian version does not identify or date this pressing. The examined label does not name Edition Karl Brüll; the publisher credit rests on a separate printed source.

additionalLinks.label: R. Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 6, p. 736

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain by Siegfried Arno. “Ach, Otto, Otto…!” Foxtrot. Electrola EG 2135 A, matrix BD 9264-2; issued January 1931. Discographic entry in Henry König’s Electrola label list, citing Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst, vol. 1, p. 27.
sources.title: Ach, Otto, Otto…! — Electrola EG 2135
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Siegfried Arno, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: The primary link leads directly to Henry König’s Electrola label list. Its EG 2135 A entry names Marek Weber and Siegfried Arno, matrix BD 9264-2, duration 3:12, the Beethoven-Saal in Berlin, release in January 1931 and the alternative issue HMV AM 3450. It cites Discographie der deutschen Kleinkunst, vol. 1, p. 27. The session field supplies a venue but no recording date; January 1931 is therefore an issue month, not a session date. The corresponding listening reference does not independently establish the pressing or take reproduced.

sources.fullCitation: HeadHunter131, uploader. “Siegfried Arno: Ach Otto Otto!” YouTube audio reference, uploaded 11 August 2008.
sources.title: Siegfried Arno: Ach Otto Otto! — Sig Arno, YouTube
sources.creator: HeadHunter131
sources.researchNote: The description identifies Marek Weber mit seinem Tanz-Orchester, Siegfried Arno and Electrola, and gives 1930 without specifying recording or issue. It supplies no catalogue or matrix number. The separate discographic source SRC0743 documents Electrola EG 2135 A, matrix BD 9264-2, issued in January 1931; that entry does not identify the pressing or take reproduced in this upload. No claim that Arno made only one performance of the song is established here.

sources.shortCitation: Electrola E.G. 2532, “Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden”
sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester. “Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden.” Fox-trot with refrain vocal; music by Walter Jurmann and Bronislaw Kaper, words by Fritz Rotter. Electrola E.G. 2532. YouTube transfer by Underlabelcrack; the uploader reports matrix OD 879-2 and a Berlin recording session around March 1932.
sources.title: Ganz ohne Liebe wär’ das Leben so bescheiden — Electrola E.G. 2532
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester
sources.researchNote: R. Pfau’s Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 3, printed p. 321, independently lists this title, its Kaper–Jurmann/Rotter credit, the film Skandal in der Parkstraße and “EG 2532 Marek Weber”. Its general year 1932 is not a separately documented issue or session date. The approximate March 1932 Berlin session and matrix OD 879-2 remain uploader-supplied. The uploader tentatively names the refrain singer as “John Hendrick”; this is not treated as a confirmed singer identification. The particular transferred pressing and take remain unverified.

additionalLinks.label: R. Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 3, p. 321
